text: Jaffle Shop stores money as integer cents. Every model that touches money needs to convert cents to dollars the same way, every time — which is exactly what a shared macro library is for.

cents_to_dollars is a real dbt macro, called from any model exactly like a built-in function. One definition means one place to get the divisor right, instead of three separate models each risking a different mistake.

payment_method_is_valid defines what counts as a valid payment method once. Reusing it in both a model and a future custom test means the two can never quietly drift apart on what valid actually means.

A third macro, date_spine_days, wraps the real dbt_utils date_spine macro with a simpler call signature, useful anywhere a mart needs one row per calendar day without re-deriving the right arguments from scratch.

A shared macro is a governance tool, not just a convenience — a single, version-controlled definition of a business rule. Next: putting this platform's narrow staging design to a real test, a late-breaking schema change.
